transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-04
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Sofia Ramos (Redwood SE), Jasmine Lee (Finlytics Head of ML), Carlos Mendes (Finlytics Platform), Priya Singh (Finlytics Security), Ahmed Noor (Finlytics Product)

Summary:
Customer wants a short 2-week POC to validate latency/cost targets for an LLM-powered analytics chat feature, agree success criteria and reporting formats. Focus on three workloads: interactive chat (short gen), long-form generation (reports), and bulk embeddings for search. Discussed go/no-go thresholds, instrumentation, and timelines.

Topics:
- Success criteria (latency p95, throughput, quality/regression thresholds)
- Workload sizing and data slices
- Benchmarks and test harness (who runs what)
- Reporting format (CSV + dashboard + per-prompt evals)
- Timeline and signoff conditions

Action items (recorded in transcript):
- Redwood to share config, harness, and pricing
- Customer to share sample prompts + security requirements

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to run through the POC success criteria and make sure we're aligned on what constitutes a sign-off. Uh, Maya from Redwood, Ethan on the line, Sofia as well.
[00:22] Jasmine: Hi all, thanks. Quick context, we're trying to add a conversational analytics assistant into our dashboard, needs to be secure for finan- for financial data and quick enough for interactive use. Timeline wise product wants a go/no-go in two weeks.
[00:40] Ethan: Got it, thanks. Quick question on current infra - are you planning to use Redwood Hosted or Dedicated/private?
[00:52] Carlos: We're leaning towards Dedicated or Private VPC, due to PCI-ish compliance. We want predictable throughput; spikes during end-of-day batch are a concern.
[01:05] Priya: Also want KMS integration and audit logs; SOC2 is a must. We'll share the audit contact.
[01:18] Maya: Perfect, that's helpful. For the POC we typically scope three benchmark buckets: 1) Interactive chat, 2) Long-form generation for report drafts, 3) Embeddings for semantic search. Does that align?
[01:35] Jasmine: Yes that sounds right. For interactive we care about p95 latency for 256 tokens, for long-form we care about throughput and stability.
[01:44] Ethan: For specifics we propose: interactive p95 < 200ms - or is that 200 or 300? sorry, let me be clear - p95 < 300ms for 256 tokens on a dedicated config, and p99 < 600ms as a stretch. Also throughput of 80-100 req/s sustained for the chat workload.
[02:05] Jasmine: 300ms p95 is aggressive but acceptable if cost isn't crazy. We need to balance. Our product goal is sub-500ms ideally.
[02:16] Sofia: To make comparisons fair we'll run the same prompt set across options and quantify latency and token cost. We'll also produce per-prompt stat CSVs and a dashboard.
[02:30] Carlos: On workload sizing, we have about 1200 daily active power users, peak 600 concurrent sessions during reports. For POC we'll simulate 100 req/s with realistic token distributions. We'll send sample logs.
[02:47] Ethan: That helps. For embeddings: need bulk embed rate and cost-per-embed; we can measure throughput and recommend batching. For long-form generation, we'll run 1k-token sequences to check stability.
[03:05] Jasmine: Success criteria table would help. We want go/no-go thresholds for latency, cost-per-100k tokens, and quality. How do you propose we measure quality?
[03:18] Maya: Good question. We usually do a combo: automated evals on a labeled prompt set (e.g., accuracy/F1 for extraction tasks) + human review for a small sample (20-30 prompts) with rubric. We can set a qualitative acceptance threshold like 4/5 average on rubric and automated F1 > 0.80 for key extraction tasks.
[03:40] Priya: For security acceptance, we require KMS, VPC peering, SSO/SAML and audit logs present in the POC environment. Those must be validated pre-signoff.
[03:54] Jasmine: Ok, let's draft final success criteria: interactive p95 < 300ms for 256 tokens, p99 < 600ms; throughput 80 req/s; long-gen stable at 1k tokens with <5% error rate; embedding throughput >5000 embeds/min with cost target <$0.25 per 1k embeds. Quality F1 >0.80 and human rubric >=4/5. Security checks: KMS, SAML, audit logs. If we pass all -> sign-off.
[04:22] Ethan: We'll codify that into a spreadsheet and attach to the POC config. We'll also version the model - recommend a curated open model or a quantized variant for Dedicated.
[04:38] Ahmed: On reporting format, product prefers weekly CSV with per-prompt metrics plus a link to a Grafana-like dashboard. Include breakdown by token cost, latency percentiles, errors and top-failed prompts.
[04:55] Sofia: We'll provide: 1) raw CSVs per-run, 2) an HTML/permalink dashboard snapshot, 3) a summary slide deck with go/no-go verdict and recommended config.
[05:08] Jasmine: Who runs the benchmarks? Will Redwood run them or will we?
[05:14] Maya: Redwood can run the harness against your sample data in our sandbox or provide the test harness and scripts so you can run locally. We recommend Redwood-run first to baseline, then customer-run for verification.
[05:27] Carlos: We'll take the harness and run within our VPC for security tests; but need Redwood to run the initial latency/cost runs to identify config.
[05:36] Ethan: Sounds good. We'll need network egress estimates, token distributions, prompt set, and a small holdout set for quality evals.
[05:48] Priya: Also can you share SOC2 and encryption docs? We'll need them for our security review.
[05:55] Maya: Yes, I'll share the security pack and SOC2 report.
[06:02] Jasmine: Timeline check - product needs go/no-go in 2 weeks. Can we fit integration + at least one full benchmark run in that window?
[06:11] Ethan: Proposed timeline: Day 0-2 integration + env setup, Day 3-6 Redwood-run benchmarks and initial tuning, Day 7 customer-run verification and security validation, Day 8-10 human evals + reporting, Day 11 final sign-off meeting. That fits ~11 days.
[06:28] Ahmed: That timeline works if we get the harness and config quickly.
[06:33] Maya: We'll aim to send config template and pricing by Apr 7, and test harness by Apr 9.
[06:40] Jasmine: Ok, one more: what about comparators? We'll want a baseline against your Hosted offering and an alternative (OpenAI) to present to product.
[06:50] Sofia: We can include Redwood Hosted baseline and a raw OpenAI (or other) baseline where licensing allows. We'll note differences: latency, cost, and model variant.
[07:02] Carlos: For acceptance tests, please include reproducible run IDs and the raw CSVs. Product wants reproducible steps to re-run.
[07:12] Ethan: We'll include the harness with a run script that produces CSV and a dashboard snapshot; every run will include a run_id and seed for RNG to improve reproducibility.
[07:26] Priya: Security: during customer-run, we'll expect logs forwarded to our SIEM and that audit events are present.
[07:35] Maya: Confirmed. We'll provide instructions for SIEM ingestion for the POC environment.
[07:42] Jasmine: Great. Let's walk through the acceptance thresholds briefly and I'll take notes.
[07:47] Jasmine: (reads) Interactive: p95 < 300ms for 256 tokens; p99 < 600ms. Throughput: 80 req/s sustained for 15 minutes. Long-gen: 1k tokens, error rate <5%. Embeddings: >5k embeds/min with per-1k cost <$0.25. Quality: automated F1 >0.80 for extraction tasks; human rubric >=4/5. Security: KMS, SAML, audit logs present. Does that reflect?
[08:12] Ethan: Yep, that's what we'll put in the success criteria spreadsheet.
[08:16] Maya: Any objections or additions?
[08:18] Priya: We'll add data residency note: logs must remain in our EU region for POC.
[08:23] Maya: Noted, we'll ensure region pinned.
[08:26] Ahmed: For reporting cadence, weekly CSV and a mid-poc check-in on Apr 15.
[08:33] Maya: We'll schedule that.
[08:36] Jasmine: Ok really appreciate the clarity. Please send the POC config and schedule.
[08:41] Maya: Action items recap: I'll send POC config, security pack, and pricing. Ethan will spin up benchmark harness. Jasmine will send sample prompts and data slices. Priya will send SOC2 contact.
[08:56] Maya: Anything else?
[09:00] Jasmine: No, that's all. Thanks everyone.
[09:05] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email and attach the spreadsheet with explicit go/no-go thresholds.
[09:12] End meeting.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., 'KV cache' transcribed as 'KV cash'), speaker overlaps and filler words present.
